dedupe_keys.name: dsnp dynamic simulator for nuclear power plants

description: DSNP (Dynamic Simulator for Nuclear Power Plants) is a system of programs and data files for simulating a nuclear power plant or parts of it. It was developed by Eric Dean at Argonne National Laboratory with sponsorship from the DOE Office of Nuclear Energy, and DOE CODE lists a release in March 1992. It comprises a block-oriented simulation language, libraries, a precompiler and a document generator: users write programs directly from plant block diagrams, and components are modules, with the reactor split into kinetics, power distribution, feedback, thermodynamic, hydraulic and decay heat modules, plus integrators, pipes and material properties. The precompiler assembles modules and data into a simulation program in Fortran. The method is location-independent. DOE CODE lists it as closed-source scientific software available by contacting Argonne's copyright office. Caveats: the software dates from 1992 and no documentation is openly linked. Simulation uses are dynamic plant simulation for transient and failure analysis. Related records: none linked on the provider's pages read on the day.
inputs: Power plant block diagrams and flow charts written as DSNP statements
